newsitem.title: UK: UK venture trusts seek 300 mln stg before end year.
newsitem.headline: UK venture trusts seek 300 mln stg before end year.

text.p: British venture capital trusts are currently raising funds of around 300 million stg as they seek to capitalise on tax planning before the end of the tax year in early April and the general election soon afterwards.

The British Venture Capital Association (BVCA) said seven new VCTs, and eight existing ones, were in the process of raising funds. The new VCTs will seek a London Stock Exchange listing following the fund-raising.
David Thorp, BVCA Smaller Companies Committee chairman, told Reuters on Friday the trusts were seeing strong levels of activity as the end of the tax year loomed on April 5.
VCTs offer a variety of tax breaks, including income and capital gains tax (CGT) relief providing they invest 70 percent of funds in smaller unquoted companies within three years of inception.
About two thirds of British jobs and around 58 percent of private sector turnover rely on companies with fewer than 500 employees.
The BVCA said the 12 established VCTs had raised over 160 million stg since they were launched, of which 43 million was in investments that qualified for the tax breaks.

The seven new VCTs seeking funds are Murray VCT 2, Oxford Technology, Close Brothers Protected, Downing Healthcare Protected, Enterprise Trust, Pennine AIM VCT II, and Protection Income & Partnership.
They are seeking between five and 50 million stg each.

Analysts say investors are looking to maximise relief ahead of an expected Labour election victory, when possible tightening of CGT could mean the current tax year provided the best opportunity to take advantage of the breaks.
They said a possible move by Labour would be to tighten current rules on reinvestment relief, where CGT relief is given on realising a previous investment if the profit is invested in a VCT.
